section.sectionSummaryBrief: Introductory heading for the maamar from Acharon Shel Pesach 5739.
section.t: With the help of Heaven.
Acharon Shel Pesach 5739*

section.sectionSummaryBrief: Explains the Zohar's question on the plural "days" in the verse, and the answer that all days from the Exodus until the future redemption are days of leaving Egypt.
section.t: "As the days of your going out from the land of Egypt, I will show him wonders."
And the Rebbe, my father-in-law, the Rebbe, brings in his maamar beginning with the words "This"
the precise point of the Zohar
regarding that which is stated "as the days" in the plural,
[for] the Exodus from Egypt was in one day
(in one moment they went out),
and likewise regarding the remembrance of the redemption from Egypt it is written
"in order that you remember the day of your going out from the land of Egypt"
(day, in the singular),
so why is it stated here "as the days" in the plural?
And he explains,
that all the days from the time of the Exodus from Egypt until the future redemption are "days of your going out from the land of Egypt,"
therefore it says "as the days" in the plural.
And it can be said,
that what is said in the maamar, that all the days from the time of the Exodus from Egypt until the future redemption are "days of your going out from the land of Egypt,"
is
because Egypt is
from the term "straits" and "boundary,"
and the concept of the Exodus from Egypt is the departure from all straits and boundaries,
even from the most sublime straits and limitations.
And this is that all these days are "days of your going out from the land of Egypt,"
that on each and every day one goes out from more sublime straits and boundaries,
until they come to the true and complete redemption through our righteous Moshiach,
for then there will be the departure from all straits and limitations,
even from the most sublime.
For regarding Moshiach it is written
"the breaker has gone up before them,"
breaking through all barriers, measures, and limitations.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: Explains that the verse speaks of the future redemption, requiring the plural "days" because the complete Exodus is achieved through daily departures from increasingly sublime limitations.
section.t: And he continues in the maamar,
that "I will show him wonders" refers to the revelation of the future redemption,
that the future redemption will also be on this level
except that it is on a more sublime level.
And it can be said,
that this continuation in the maamar, that "I will show him wonders" refers to the revelation of the future redemption,
is in order to explain
(more)
the reason for that which is stated in this verse "as the days of your going out from the land of Egypt"
("as the days" in the plural),
even though regarding the obligation to remember the redemption from Egypt it is written "in order that you remember the day of your going out from the land of Egypt"
("day" in the singular).
Because since it speaks of the future redemption
("I will show him wonders"),
for then there will be the perfection of the Exodus from Egypt,
the departure from all straits and limitations
(even from the most sublime straits and limitations),
and in order to come to this revelation it is through the service of the Exodus from Egypt that is on each and every day,
that on each and every day one goes out from more sublime straits
(as above),
therefore it says "as the days" in the plural.
For the concept of the Exodus from Egypt through which they will come to the future redemption is the departure from Egypt the first time
(in one day)
[for this too pertains to the future redemption,
and as it is stated in the maamar
that in the redemption from Egypt the entire concept of redemption was renewed and the channel was opened for all redemptions
(from the exiles after the exile of Egypt),
also for the future redemption],
and the departure from the straits and limitations after the departure from Egypt
(in its simple sense),
that each day one goes out from more sublime straits,
until through all this they will reach the future redemption, when there will be the Exodus from Egypt in its ultimate perfection,
the departure from all straits and limitations.
